channel.title: Dylan Gaeta: News
channel.description: Research, fieldwork, conferences, teaching, and milestones from Dylan Gaeta, Ph.D.

item.title: Launched snowdrought.org
item.description: Registered the domain on October 2 and launched snowdrought.org, the Western US Climate and Snow Drought Explorer. An interactive research dashboard with maps, time series, seasonal cycles, and cross-product anomalies of snow, water, carbon, and vegetation across the Western U.S. (1990–2026). Built from the same multi-dataset analysis behind my postdoc research on snow drought and the carbon cycle.

item.title: CIRES Science Summit

item.title: Paper published: U.S. oil and gas methane intensity, 2019–2024
item.description: Our paper U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact came out in Communications Earth & Environment. Led by Ao Chen in the Greenhouse Gas Lab.

item.title: OCO-2 v11 MIP modeling workshop
item.description: Joined the OCO-2 v11 Model Intercomparison Project (MIP) modeling workshop with the atmospheric CO₂ flux inversion groups that assimilate OCO-2 retrievals. The MIP compares global flux estimates across inversion systems, including CarbonTracker from NOAA GML and CU Boulder.

item.title: GMAC 2026 poster: methyl bromide emissions
item.description: Presented A decline but no cessation of methyl bromide emissions from the United States over 2007–2018 at GMAC 2026, the 53rd NOAA Global Monitoring Annual Conference (abstract volume). Used tall tower, observatory, and aircraft flask-sample measurements of CH₃Br from the NOAA GGGRN with a geostatistical inverse model to estimate U.S. emissions across the Montreal Protocol phase-out years.

item.description: Attended the third annual Johns Hopkins Science Diplomacy Summit, which brought together government officials, researchers, and industry on AI, quantum, climate innovation, health, space, Arctic science, and research security.

CIRES profile

item.title: Defended my dissertation
item.description: Defended U.S. emissions of trace gas air pollutants inferred from a long-term atmospheric measurement network: from fumigants to fossil fuels. Three case studies, each using NOAA GML flask measurements and a geostatistical inverse model to map U.S. emissions, trends, and uncertainties: Sulfuryl fluoride: California dominates U.S. emissions, mostly from structural fumigation of western drywood termites. Methyl bromide: emissions fell after the Montreal Protocol phase-out but not to zero, sustained by quarantine and pre-shipment uses and California strawberry growing. Propane, butane, and pentane: oil and gas basins dominate, led by the Permian, Anadarko, Eagle Ford, and Haynesville, with implications for ozone downwind. Common thread: large discrepancies between top-down and bottom-up estimates. The public defense ran 1:30–2:30 pm with a Zoom option; the department announced it in the Monday Minute. Since Prof. Ben Hobbs couldn't be there, I offered to give an abridged version in his Energy & Environment Systems Seminar.

item.title: Invited to peer review a California Council on Science and Technology report

CCST is the nonpartisan nonprofit created by the California Legislature to bring science expertise to state policymaking.

item.title: First first-author paper: sulfuryl fluoride
item.description: Published California dominates U.S. emissions of the pesticide and potent greenhouse gas sulfuryl fluoride in Communications Earth & Environment. Using NOAA GGGRN measurements and a geostatistical inverse model, we found California emits 60–85% of U.S. SO₂F₂ (0.26 ± 0.10 Gg/yr), equal to 5.5–12% of global emissions. Accepted on February 28 after a long road through several journals (see June 2023); coordinated an embargoed press release with the journal and the JHU Hub, and the paper went live on April 3. Fielded interview requests from the Los Angeles Times, Inside Climate News, and Southern California Public Radio, and recorded audio for Sea Change Radio. Coverage followed in The Guardian, Scientific American, The Hill, the San Francisco Chronicle, and Courthouse News (all media).
